title: EOF at the interactive fresh-state prompt escapes as an uncaught traceback
reasoning: When stdin is a TTY, input() can raise EOFError, such as when the operator presses Ctrl-D. Neither _resolve_fresh_mode nor main handles EOFError, so a routine refusal/closed-input condition produces a traceback rather than retaining state and stopping cleanly.
reproduction: Run against clean existing ClawPatch state in a terminal without --fresh or --resume-stopped, then press Ctrl-D at the fresh-state prompt.
recommendation: Treat EOF as a negative answer or convert it to a controlled SafetyError explaining that existing state was retained.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests cover EOF or closed-input behavior at the interactive prompt.
suggestedRegressionTest: Patch input to raise EOFError and assert that main retains existing state, emits a controlled message, and returns the documented nonzero status without a traceback.
minimumFixScope: Handle EOFError around the fresh-state input call and add one CLI regression test.

history.reasoning: The original prompt moved from lines 80–89 to lines 86–92. It now catches EOFError and raises a controlled SafetyError stating that existing state was retained; main catches SafetyError at lines 520–523, prints STOPPED, and returns 2. Commit 0ab6d1b contains this repair, README documentation, and a regression test at tests/test_cli.py:873–897 asserting exit 2, no sweep invocation, the controlled message, and no traceback. The targeted regression passed. The first full-suite run failed only because the inherited temporary directory no longer existed; rerunning with TMPDIR=/dev/shm passed all 197 tests with 9 platform skips. The failed linked attempt is therefore superseded by current passing validation.
